headline: 9 workers killed by toxic gas; BSRB suspends operations at Ferdous Steel
summary: The Bangladesh Ship Recycling Board (BSRB) has halted activities at the Sitakunda shipyard after a hydrogen sulfide gas leak killed nine workers.
details: Nine workers died after being exposed to toxic hydrogen sulfide gas inside an LNG-carrier scrap vessel at the Ferdous Steel shipbreaking yard in Bhatiari, Sitakunda, Chattogram.

Among the victims was Abdul Alim Sujon, a 35-year-old safety and environment assistant. His father reported that Sujon rushed into the vessel to rescue fellow workers and managed to save one person before being overcome by the gas.
Sujon's family, including his wife and two children, has urged the company to provide financial support, stating that the authorities are responsible for workplace safety.
Family members and colleagues alleged a severe lack of safety measures, claiming there was insufficient equipment, no proper rescue plan, and that the exit door was locked during the leak.
The Bangladesh Ship Recycling Board (BSRB) has since suspended operations at the yard to investigate the tragedy.
The victims' families and local residents are demanding an impartial investigation into the management's negligence.
caption:
A safety officer rushed in to save his colleagues, but toxic gas claimed his life along with 8 others.

Nine workers died after being exposed to toxic hydrogen sulfide gas inside an LNG-carrier scrap vessel at the Ferdous Steel shipbreaking yard in Bhatiari, Sitakunda, Chattogram.

Among the victims was Abdul Alim Sujon, a 35-year-old safety and environment assistant. His father reported that Sujon rushed into the vessel to rescue fellow workers and managed to save one person before being overcome by the gas.

Sujon's family, including his wife and two children, has urged the company to provide financial support, stating that the authorities are responsible for workplace safety.

Family members and colleagues alleged a severe lack of safety measures, claiming there was insufficient equipment, no proper rescue plan, and that the exit door was locked during the leak.

The Bangladesh Ship Recycling Board (BSRB) has since suspended operations at the yard to investigate the tragedy.

The victims' families and local residents are demanding an impartial investigation into the management's negligence.

headline_marked: Model-actress [[Ridhika Ridhi found dead]] in Bashundhara home
headline: Model-actress Ridhika Ridhi found dead in Bashundhara home
summary: The 26-year-old actress, whose real name was Lina Akhter, was found hanging from a ceiling fan in her rented apartment.
details: Police recovered the body of model and actress Ridhika Ridhi from a house in Dhaka’s Bashundhara residential area this morning.
Bhatara Police Station OC Mazharul Islam stated that police arrived at the residence around 6:00 am and found the woman's body hanging from a ceiling fan.
The victim's real name was Lina Akhter, and she was 26 years old. She had rented the apartment in Bashundhara on her own.
According to a relative, Ridhi was her stage name. The victim's family is now preparing to file an abetment of suicide case in connection with the incident.
caption:
A 26-year-old model and actress has been found dead in her Bashundhara home.

Police recovered the body of model and actress Ridhika Ridhi from a house in Dhaka’s Bashundhara residential area this morning.

Bhatara Police Station OC Mazharul Islam stated that police arrived at the residence around 6:00 am and found the woman's body hanging from a ceiling fan.

The victim's real name was Lina Akhter, and she was 26 years old. She had rented the apartment in Bashundhara on her own.

According to a relative, Ridhi was her stage name. The victim's family is now preparing to file an abetment of suicide case in connection with the incident.
